title: In re Kuvara, Attorney at Law
State v. Votava
questions: Whether a person charged with being in actual physical control of a vehicle while intoxicated can use the statutory defense of moving the vehicle “safely off the roadway” if another person drove the vehicle off the road.

title: In re Court
questions: Whether censure and a 120 day suspension is the appropriate disciplinary sanction for a judge pro tempore who believed he could accept guilty pleas from defendants whom he had represented as a public defender and who used defective guilty plea forms supplied by the court he was temporarily serving.

title: Washington Independent Telephone Association on behalf of itself and its member companies, and CenturyTel of Washington , a Washington corporation, CenturyTel of Cowiche , a Washington corporation, McDaniel Telephone Company, a Washington corporation, Lewis River Telephone Company, a Washington corporation, Inland Telephone Company, a Washington corporation, Ellensburg Telephone Company, a Washington corporation, Kalama Telephone Company, a Washington corporation, Western Wahkiakum County Telephone Company, a Washington corporation, and The Toledo Telephone Company , a Washington corporation, Petitioners, v. Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission, Respondent, United States Cellular Corporation, Intervenor
questions: Whether the Washington State Utilities and Transportation Commission, by designating a telecommunications company as eligible for federal funding to support universal services, violated any interest of other eligible carriers protected by the Due Process Clause, or acted arbitrarily or capriciously.

title: In re Rideout
questions: What is the proper appellate standard of review where a trial court’s decision is based solely on documentation, including declarations, and where the credibility of the parties is at issue before the court. Additionally, whether a divorced parent may be held in contempt for bad faith violation of a parenting plan when a child refuses visitation with the noncustodial parent.

title: State v. 12/18/84
questions: Whether evidence of the defendant’s drug possession, found in his home, should have been suppressed because police officers who went to his home to talk with him about an unrelated crime failed to inform his grandmother, who answered the door, that she did not have to let them in and could revoke her consent at any time.

title: Judy Kloepfel, Respondent, v. Joseph Bokor, Petitioner
questions: Whether a plaintiff must present medical evidence of objective physical symptoms or manifestations of severe emotional injury in order to prevail on a claim for intentional infliction of emotional distress.

title: State v. Moen
questions: Whether a prosecutor may condition plea bargaining on a defendant’s waiver of the right to request the identity of a confidential informant in a related civil action seeking return of forfeited property.

title: In re An, Attorney at Law
In re Miller, Attorney at Law
In re Whitt, Attorney at Law
State v. State
questions: Whether an officer may request the identification of a passenger in a lawfully stopped vehicle absent an articulable suspicion of criminal activity or other reasonable rationale for doing so without violating the passenger's right to privacy pursuant to Washington Constitution, article I, section 7.

title: In re Washington
questions: Whether convictions for both vehicular homicide and second degree felony murder based on the same death violate the Double Jeopardy Clause, and whether the petitioner was procedurally barred from making that argument in a personal restraint petition, when that issue was raised and rejected on direct appeal. Whether the felony murder conviction should be vacated because the defendant pled guilty to vehicular homicide before trial on the felony murder charge.

title: Tex Enterprises , a Washington corporation, Respondent, v. Brockway Standard , a foreign corporation, and J.F. Shelton Company, a Washington corporation, Petitioners
questions: Whether a manufacturer’s representations about its product to a commercial buyer can create an implied warranty to the buyer, where the buyer purchases the product from a third party distributor and there is no contract between the manufacturer and the buyer.

title: In re Cohen, Attorney at Law
State v. Tilton
questions: Whether the record in this juvenile’s trial was insufficient for appeal and requires reversal of his conviction when the defendant’s trial testimony was not recorded, the parties did not follow the procedures set forth in RAP 9.3-9.5 in reconstructing the record, and the defendant was not represented in the reconstruction of the record.

title: City of Redmond, Petitioner, v. Juan Arroyo-Murillo, Respondent
questions: Whether the trial court properly dismissed this prosecution for driving with a suspended license on the ground that the predicate suspension violated due process because the Department of Licensing mailed its revocation order only to an address it obtained from a traffic citation rather than to the address provided to the Department by the license holder.

title: City of Redmond, Appellant, v. Dean A. Moore, Respondent. City of Redmond, Appellant, v. Jason D. Wilson, Respondent
questions: Whether the trial court properly dismissed these prosecutions for driving with a suspended license on the ground that the license suspension procedure of RCW 46.20.289 and .291 violates due process because it affords no opportunity for a hearing before the Department of Licensing.

title: Paul Plein, Respondent, v. Chester Lackey and Lee Cameron, Jane Doe Cameron and their marital community, Petitioners
questions: Whether the corporate officer who signed the corporation’s promissory note signed it as an accommodation party who, upon his payment of the note, was entitled to foreclose a deed of trust securing the debt, and, whether challenges to the foreclosure proceedings were waived.

title: State v. Wentz
questions: Whether for purposes of the first degree burglary statute a fenced back yard qualifies as a “building” by virtue of being a “fenced area,” without regard to the uses of the area.

title: In re Beckmann
questions: Whether stock purchased during marriage by exercising a community option using separate funds should at dissolution be characterized as community property, separate property, or a mixture of both, and whether the increased value of the stock should be apportioned based on the ownership interests when it was purchased.

title: State v. Rohrich
questions: Whether the Court of Appeals properly upheld the dismissal of this child molestation prosecution pursuant to CrR 8.3(b), on the ground that the delay in bringing the charge may have allowed witnesses’ memories to fade and the defendant’s own recall of the incident to be compromised.

title: Clark County Public Utility District No. 1, Respondent, v. International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, Petitioner
questions: Whether a labor arbitrator’s conclusions were reversible as arbitrary and capricious, or otherwise outside the arbitrator’s authority, when the arbitrator interpreted a collective bargaining agreement to include parts of a personnel policy manual.

title: Sunnyside Valley Irrigation District, a quasi-municipal corporation, Respondent, v. Dyke Dickie and Jane Doe Dickie, husband and wife, Petitioners
questions: Whether the terms of an easement permit the grantee to increase the width of their right of way to accommodate larger and more efficient maintenance equipment and to support increased demands on the irrigation ditch from effluent produced by the upstream irrigation sources?

title: City of Seattle, Respondent, v. Andrew Guay, Petitioner
questions: Whether, for purposes of meeting rule-based speedy trial deadlines, authorities bringing criminal charges in courts of limited jurisdiction have the authority to issue a transfer order to secure the presence of defendants who are incarcerated in other counties.

title: Keith A. Pacheco, Petitioner, v. John R. Ames, D.D.S., a sole proprietor, Respondent, Thomas F. Whitfield, D.D.S., a sole proprietor, Defendant
questions: Whether, in this action for dental malpractice, the trial court erred in giving a res ipsa loquitur instruction when there was evidence that the injury could have occurred without negligence on the defendant’s part.

title: State v. Ackerman
questions: Whether, for purposes of meeting rule-based speedy trial deadlines, authorities bringing criminal charges in courts of limited jurisdiction have the authority to issue a transfer order to secure the presence of defendants who are incarcerated in other counties.

title: State v. Hardesty
questions: Whether, when a criminal charge is first filed in district court and later filed in superior court, the “time elapsed in district court” for purposes of the speedy trial period includes time spent in jail in another county on an unrelated matter.

title: State v. Kindsvogel
questions: Whether the defendant’s conviction for manufacturing marijuana must be overturned pursuant to CrR 4.3.1, the joinder of charges rule, because the state had earlier prosecuted him for domestic violence, after his wife told a police officer that he had assaulted her and also was growing marijuana.

title: In re Brothers, Attorney at Law
In re Hankerson
questions: Whether, in this prosecution for aggravated first degree murder, the trial court erred in its accomplice liability instructions and in admitting a co-defendant’s “whole” statement against penal interest, and if so, whether the defendant, as a personal restraint petitioner, has established prejudice.

title: State v. Smith
questions: Whether the federal or Washington Constitution requires a jury (rather than the sentencing judge) to determine whether the state has proven the prior convictions necessary to sentence a defendant to life without the possibility of parole under the Persistent Offender Accountability Act.

title: State v. Swenson
questions: Whether the defendant was timely arraigned, where he was in custody in another county when charged and was not arraigned until 149 days after pleading guilty to the other county’s charges.

title: In re Turay
questions: Whether, in this proceeding to commit the petitioner as a sexually violent predator, instituted after his 18-month parole for a sex crime had recently been revoked, the State was required to plead and prove a “recent overt act.”

title: The City of Seattle, a municipal corporation, Respondent, v. Rory Crispin and Jane Doe Crispin, husband and wife and the marital community composed thereof, Petitioners
questions: Whether the division of land that created a lot qualified as a boundary line adjustment for purposes of the exemption from the platting/subdivision statutes set forth in RCW 58.17.040(6).

title: In re Kagele, Attorney at Law
In re Ryan
questions: Whether the defendant should have been informed that the crime to which she was pleading guilty rendered her ineligible for early release credits for five years, and if so, whether, in seeking to withdraw her plea, she must show that failure to inform her of that consequence affected her plea decision.

title: State v. Turley
questions: Whether the defendant, who pleaded guilty to charges of escape and conspiracy without being informed that the conspiracy conviction required community placement upon release from prison, should be allowed to withdraw only the guilty plea to the conspiracy conviction or the entire plea agreement.

title: State v. J.P.
questions: Whether a juvenile court may order an offender to pay restitution for the costs of a victim’s crime-related counseling in a non-sex offense case. See RCW 13.40.190(1); RCW 13.40.020(22).

title: State v. Baldwin
questions: Whether the defendant’s convictions for identity theft and forgery violate state and federal double jeopardy protections. Additionally, whether the statutes that authorized the defendant’s exceptional sentences, RCW 9.94A.120 and RCW 9.94A.390, are unconstitutionally vague and thus violate her due process rights.

title: State v. Deryke
questions: Whether the “to convict” instruction on a charge of attempted first degree rape was inadequate because it failed to specify the degree of rape allegedly attempted.

title: State v. Snedden
questions: Whether indecent exposure is “a crime against a person” that can support a charge of second degree burglary under RCW 9A.52.030(1).

title: American Continental Insurance Company, Plaintiff-Appellee, v. Susan Steen, individually and as personal representative for the Estate of Steven Steen, Defendant-Appellant
questions: Whether a hospital’s cancellation of “claims-made” insurance policies that would have covered the hospital’s liability to a patient for a pre-cancellation injury was a retroactive annulment of insurance prohibited by RCW 48.18.320 or by public policy.

title: Butzberger v. State
questions: Whether a driver who was killed when he got out of his car to go to the aid of a person trapped inside an overturned truck was “using” the overturned truck and/or his own car, for the purposes of underinsured motorist insurance.

title: Shulamit Glaubach, Dawn Merydith, Kristen Tsiatsios, and all persons similarly situated, Plaintiff, v. Regence Blueshield, a Washington corporation Defendant
questions: Shulamit Glaubach sued Regence Blue Shield, her health insurer, for not covering prescription birth control. She argues that is illegal discrimination.

title: State v. Thomas
questions: Covell Paul Thomas appeals his conviction for aggravated first degree murder and his sentence of death. He contends that the trial court made several incorrect rulings during jury selection as well as numerous erroneous evidentiary rulings. Thomas also argues that erroneous jury instructions given during his trial violated his constitutional rights. title: In re Services
questions: Whether, following termination of parental rights to a child, the child’s grandparents have standing to petition for the child’s adoption and should be given preference in the adoption decision.

title: State v. DeVincentis
questions: Louis DeVincentis argues he should get a new trial because the State did not show that the evidence of his plan to molest children was unique or uncommon.

title: In re Roach
questions: Whether a prisoner who is mistakenly released and later returned to prison is entitled to credit against his or her sentence for time spent at liberty.

title: State v. Redmond
questions: In 2001, Mr. Redmond was involved in a fight at Lindbergh High School in Renton. The State charged him with criminal assault. Mr. Redmond claims he acted in self defense. Three issues are presented. First, whether the trial court erred by refusing to give the jury a no duty to retreat instruction. Second, whether the trial court erred by admitting medical records that contained a vivid description of the high school fight. Finally, whether the trial court erred by admitting statements that the victim heard from other students that Mr. Redmond had been looking for him.

title: Jolynn R. Barrett, individually, and Jolynn R. Barrett, as guardian ad litem for Jessica J. Barrett and Jaleen A. Barrett, minors, Plaintiffs, v. Lucky 7 Saloon , formerly a Washington corporation;, and L2S , d/b/a Lucky 7 Saloon, a Washington corporation, Defendants. Jeffrey A. Barrett and John R. Barrett, Jr., as limited guardian of the person and estate of Jeffrey A. Barrett, a person in need of assistance, Petitioners, v. Lucky Seven Saloon , a Washington corporation formerly dba Lucky Seven Saloon; L2S , a Washington corporation dba Lucky Seven Saloon; Anthony Joyce and Gilda Joyce, and the marital community comprised thereof; Roger Morse and Luane Morse, and the marital community comprised thereof, Respondents
questions: Whether RCW 66.44.200(1), which prohibits the sale of alcohol to “any person apparently under the influence of liquor,” establishes a standard of liability in civil actions for damages caused by intoxicated drivers.

title: State v. Garza
questions: Benjamin Garza was on his way to the third day of his trial for eluding police in a high speed chase when he was arrested on an unrelated charge. Not knowing where Garza was, the trial judge decided to continue without him, which Garza claims violated his constitutional right to be present at trial.

title: Dougherty v. State
questions: If a worker files his worker's compensation appeal in the wrong county and the deadline for filing the appeal has passed, does the worker's compensation law allow him to move his appeal to the proper county or does it bar the worker from moving it after the deadline?

title: State v. Dhaliwal
questions: Did an attorney improperly represent both the defendant and several of the witnesses at the defendant’s trial?

title: State v. Jackson
questions: Defendant Jackson, who was convicted of murdering his daughter, argues that the State illegally obtained evidence by using a global positioning device attached to his truck to track his movements.

title: State v. State
questions: Whether the two defendants were properly convicted of homicide by abuse of the 23-month old victim.

title: City of Seattle v. State
questions: Whether a city may legally shift the cost of operating streetlights from the city budget’s general fund to the city’s electrical utility and its customers.

title: Rud Okeson, Doris Burns, Walter L. Williams and Arthur T. Lane, individually and on behalf of the class of all persons similarly situated, Appellants, v. The City of Seattle, Respondent
questions: Whether a city may legally shift the cost of operating streetlights from the city budget’s general fund to the city’s electrical utility and its customers.

title: State v. Goldberg
questions: Goldberg was convicted of the aggravated murder of his son-in-law, who was killed to prevent him from testifying in a case Goldberg was not a party to. He now argues that the charge was improper and the jury was coerced.

title: American States Insurance Company, Respondent, v. Symes of Silverdale , et al., Defendants, Kathryn Ellis, as bankruptcy trustee, Petitioner
questions: Whether a bankruptcy trustee who left the debtor corporation in possession can recover insurance proceeds for a fire at the debtor’s premises when the debtor could not do so because the fire was intentionally caused by a corporate officer.

title: In re An, Attorney at Law
Janice M. Smith and Randal Smith, individually and as assignees, Petitioners, v. Safeco Insurance Company and Linda Bryce, individually, Respondents
questions: Whether an insurer breached the duty of good faith that it owed to its insured by not complying with a third-party claimant’s demand, made before any lawsuit was filed, for the disclosure of the insured’s policy limits. 1:00 P.M. -

title: In re Grasso
questions: Vincent Grasso was convicted of sexually abusing his five-year-old daughter. He now argues that the trial judge improperly admitted into evidence several of the child’s out-of-court statements describing the abuse.

title: Washington Employers Concerned About Regulating Ergonomics, et al., Appellants, v. Department of Labor and Industries, et al., Respondents
questions: A business collation challenges workplace ergonomic rules enacted by the Department of Labor and Industries, arguing the rules are unjustified and the Department failed to follow proper procedures.

title: Mike M. Johnson , a Washington corporation, Respondent, v. The County of Spokane, a Washington state municipal corporation, Petitioner
questions: In construction contracts, does an owner’s notice that the contractor has concerns and disputes excuse the contractor from complying with mandatory claim procedures under the contract? Furthermore, in this case did the Court of Appeals correctly determine that a question exists as to whether the owner intended to waive the contractor’s compliance with the contractual claim provisions.

title: State v. Thompson
questions: James Ross Thompson was convicted of manufacturing methamphetamines. He argues that the evidence used to convict him was bad because the police did not have the right to (1) open his trailer door to arrest him; (2) search the trailer; or (3) search a boathouse where they found evidence of drug manufacturing.

title: Sane Transit, a Washington non-profit corporation, and Mark Baerwaldt, for themselves and on behalf of taxpayers, Appellants, v. Sound Transit, officially known as the Central Puget Sound Regional Transit Authority, a Washington municipal corporation, Respondent
questions: Can Sound Transit build a 14-mile electric light rail line from downtown Seattle to Tukwila rather than build a 21-mile electric light rail line from the University District of Seattle to the City of SeaTac?

title: State v. Mannering
questions: Whether a person charged with attempted first degree murder can raise the defense of duress.

title: City of Seattle, Petitioner, v. Mighty Movers , Respondent
questions: Mighty Movers, Inc. challenges the City of Seattle’s ordinance banning posters on utility poles and other public property. Does Seattle’s anti-posting law violate the state constitutional right to free speech?

title: In re Washington
questions: Under a policy enacted after Steven Forbis had been convicted and imprisoned, the Department of Corrections required him to take part in stress and anger management classes. When he refused, the Department took away some of the early release credits he had earned. Forbis argues that the policy punished him retrospectively, in violation of the ex post facto clauses of the state and federal constitutions.

title: Lynda Breckenridge, et al., Petitioners, v. Valley General Hospital, et al., Respondents
questions: Lynda Breckenridge sued Dr. Nowak for medical malpractice. Was it misconduct for a member of the jury to discuss his wife’s similar symptoms during deliberations?

title: In re An, Attorney at Law
State v. Tarabochia
questions: Whether the defendant untimely filed an affidavit of prejudice against a judge in a one-judge county. 1:00 P.M.

title: Washington Education Association, on behalf of itself and its members, Respondents, v. Washington State Public Disclosure Commission, Christine Yorozu, Chair; Gerry Marsh, Lois Clement, Susan Brady, and Ronda Cahill, Commissioners of the Public Disclosure Commission, in their individual capacities, Appellants
questions: Whether the Public Disclosure Commission’s guidelines advising public school employees not to distribute information about upcoming school levies among themselves on school grounds or to use the school e-mail system for that purpose violates the employees’ constitutional free speech rights.

title: State v. them
questions: Porter was arrested and convicted of delivery of cocaine after Seattle police conducted a successful buy-bust operation. On appeal, Porter argues that the trial court and the Court of Appeals misapplied the test used to determine whether a lesser included offense instruction is appropriate.

title: In re An, Attorney at Law
State v. Cheatam
questions: The defendant, who was convicted of rape, claims that inadmissible evidence was used to convict him. 1:00 P.M.

title: State v. State
questions: The superior court said that the $30 license tab measure passed by voters in November 2002 (I-776) was unconstitutional. This court must decide whether I-776 was comprised of two unrelated laws and whether its passage substantially impaired King County's contracts with bondholders.

title: In re Washington
questions: With a few exceptions, there is a one-year time limit from the final judgment in which a criminal defendant may file a post-conviction motion or personal restraint petition. The issue in these cases is about meeting that deadline—whether paperwork filed by prisoners who do not have attorneys should be considered “filed” when deposited in the prison mailing system, or only when received by the court.

title: State v. Goins
questions: When a general verdict and special verdict stemming from one count are inconsistent, does the not guilty special verdict void the guilty general verdict?

title: State v. McLean
questions: With a few exceptions, there is a one-year time limit from the final judgment in which a criminal defendant may file a post-conviction motion or personal restraint petition. The issue in these cases is about meeting that deadline—whether paperwork filed by prisoners who do not have attorneys should be considered “filed” when deposited in the prison mailing system, or only when received by the court.

title: State v. Carter
questions: Whether two off-duty criminal investigators needed a warrant to open and inspect a gun provided to them during a private gun handling course.

title: Brooks v. State
questions: This case requires the Court to decide if an individual who is arrested under a warrant issued for someone else can sue the jail where he or she is held for failing to discover there was a misidentification.

title: Malted Mousse , a Washington corporation, Petitioner, v. Michael A. Steinmetz, Respondent
questions: Steinmetz won at arbitration but was denied his request for attorneys’ fees. The issue is whether he could appeal just the denial of attorneys’ fees or whether he had to seek a whole new trial.

title: Seattle Police Officers Guild, a Washington nonprofit corporation, Defendant, Dennis P. Ramm, Tim D. Greeley, and Keith Swank, Petitioners, v. The City of Seattle, a municipal corporation, City of Seattle Public Safety Civil Service Commission and Norm Stamper, Chief of Police of Seattle Police Department, Respondents. Dennis L. Hossfeld, Plaintiff, v. The City of Seattle, a municipal corporation, City of Seattle Public Safety Civil Service Commission and Norm Stamper, Chief of Police of Seattle Police Department, Respondents
questions: Whether the City of Seattle’s process of promoting police officers complies with the state civil service statute that requires the City to promote police officers on the basis of merit.

title: State v. Ramer
questions: Whether the trial court erred by finding the 11 year old defendant lacked the capacity to commit first degree rape of a child.

title: Norm Maleng, in his capacity as King County Prosecuting Attorney, Respondent, v. King County Corrections Guild, Appellant
questions: Whether proposed initiative measure 18, which seeks to amend the King County Charter to reduce the size of the King County Council from 13 to 9 members, can be placed on the November 2003 election ballot.

title: Restaurant Development , a Washington corporation, individually and in behalf of all others similarly situated, Petitioners, v. Cananwill , a California corporation, Respondent
questions: Did an insurance premium finance company impose a service charge that exceeded the maximum amount allowed by Washington law? If so, was this also a violation of the Consumer Protection Act?

title: Linda Blaney, Respondent, v. International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, District No. 160, Petitioners
questions: The trial court found that the District discriminated against Blaney because she is a woman. Three issues concerning the money she was awarded will be discussed today: (1) was the trial court correct in telling the jury to figure out Blaney’s future wage and benefits loss from the date of the trial until her retirement, and (2) should Blaney get more money to cover the taxes she will have to pay on the money she won and (3) to pay her attorneys for the work they did on her appeal?

title: Mount Adams School District, Respondent, v. William D. Cook; Mount Adams Education Association; and Washington Education Association, Petitioners
questions: Mount Adams School District fired William Cook, a teacher, for not having a teaching certificate on the first day of school. Mr. Cook argues that the school district’s decision to fire him must be submitted to arbitration.

title: Parkland Light & Water Co., Fruitland Mutual Water Co., Mountain View-Edgewater Water Co., Summit Water and Supply Co., and Spanaway Water Co., Appellants, v. Tacoma-Pierce County Board of Health and The Tacoma-Pierce County Health Department, Respondents. Lakewood Water District, a special purpose municipal corporation, Appellant, v. Tacoma-Pierce County Board of Health and the Tacoma-Pierce County Health Department, Respondents. Citizens Opposing Fluoridation in Pierce County, Appellant, v. Tacoma-Pierce County Board of Health and the Tacoma-Pierce County Health Department, Respondents. City of Bonney Lake, Appellant, v. Tacoma-Pierce County Board of Health and the Tacoma-Pierce County Health Department, Respondents
questions: A number of water districts challenge the Pierce County Board of Health’s regulation requiring the water districts to add fluoride to the water.

title: State ex rel. Citizens Against Tolls (CAT), a Washington non-profit corporation, Appellant, v. Michael J. Murphy, Washington State Treasurer and Chair of the Washington State Finance Committee; The Washington State Finance Committee, Douglas B. MacDonald, Secretary of Transportation; Washington State Department of Transportation, Aubrey Davis, Chair of the Washington State Transportation Commission; and the Washington State Transportation Commission, Respondents
questions: Citizens Against Tolls (CAT) challenges the State’s decision to award several contracts without a normal bidding process and to allow repayment of the motor vehicle fund that pays off state bonds with toll revenues in the Tacoma Narrows Bridge project. CAT also claims that the law allowing the Tacoma Narrows Bridge project to go forward is unconstitutional and that several errors were made by the trial judge.

title: State v. C.G.
questions: A high-school student challenges her conviction of felony harassment, on the ground that the victim did not fear that her threat to kill would be carried out.

title: State v. M.K.
questions: A middle-school student challenges his conviction of felony harassment, claiming that his statement implying a school-shooting was intended as a joke.

title: Rick Hangartner, Respondent, v. City of Seattle, Appellant. (C/A 51236-6-I and 51630-2-I) MOTION TO SUBSTITUTE NEW PAGE 50-PASSED TO THE MERITS Citizens Against the Monorail, a political action committee registered with the Washington State Public Disclosure Commission, Respondent, v. The Elevated Transportation Company, a public development agency, and Harold Robertson, Appellant
questions: This case is consolidated with the previous case, Hangartner v. City of Seattle, and the primary issues are the same.

title: Rebecca Hamm v. State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance Company, Respondent
questions: Case #1 and Case #2 share the same central issue, and are referred to as companion cases. In this case, the no-fault motorist was injured in a car accident with an uninsured motorist. The insurance company took an offset similar to the offset taken in Case #1. The motorist in this case also seeks to compel her insurance company to pay a pro rata share of her attorney fees.

title: Safeco Insurance Company, Respondent, v. Denise Brackett Woodley, Petitioner
questions: A no-fault motorist was injured in a car accident with an underinsured motorist. Her insurance company offset the amount of money owed to her under one type of coverage based on prior payments owed to her under another type of coverage. The motorist argues that because she had to pay attorneys in order to create the pool of money that allowed the insurance company to take the offset, the insurance company should pay a pro rata share of her attorney fees.

title: State v. Taylor
questions: Whether an individual, who was formally charged with a crime, may appeal an order dismissing the charge.

title: In re Petitioners
questions: Petitioners claim that the court's decision in Andress requires vacation of their second degree felony murder convictions predicated on assault.

title: State v. Hanson
questions: Appellant Hanson claims that the court's decision in Andress requires vacation of his second degree felony murder conviction predicated on assault.

title: State v. Goodman
questions: Goodman was convicted of possessing methamphetamine with intent to deliver. The charging document listed the drug as “meth” rather than the full name “methamphetamine.” The court must decide if the evidence was sufficient to support the conviction and whether the use of “meth” rather than “methamphetamine” in the charging document was improper.

title: Jerry L. Hisle, Michael D, Nicholas, Dale A. Riccetti, Jerry Roth, Ron L. Shoup, individually, and on behalf of the class they represent, Respondents, v. Todd Pacific Shipyards Corporation, a Delaware corporation, Petitioner
questions: Todd Pacific Shipyards and its employees signed an agreement stating that Todd’s employees would be paid 60¢ for every hour they worked from one date to another. Hisle is hundreds of Todd employees who feel they should be paid overtime (90¢ an hour) for the overtime hours they worked between the dates listed in the agreement. In addition to whether overtime should be paid, this case also addresses whether federal or state courts should hear this case, whether this case was already decided in a prior suit, and whether costs and attorney fees should be granted on appeal.

title: Yaeko Otani, Deceased, through her personal representative, Pauline Shigaki, Petitioner, v. David R. Broudy, M.D., Respondent
questions: This case requires the court to determine whether RCW 4.20.046, Washington’s general survival statute, allows a decedent’s estate to recover damages for a decedent’s loss of enjoyment of life, including shortened life expectancy.

title: Arborwood Idaho v. State
questions: The City of Kennewick collects a monthly ambulance charge from every household in the city. Arborwood, a non-resident owner of apartments in Kennewick, objects to the ambulance charge.

title: Gary Anderson and Amelia Anderson, husband and wife, Appellants, v. Galvin Flying Service , a Washington corporation, Respondent

John D. Carlisle (deceased), a single man by and through Delbert D. Carlisle as the personal representative of his estate; and Delbert D. Carlisle and Myrna L. Carlisle, individually, Appellants, v. Group Health Cooperative of Puget Sound and Unknown John Does, Respondents

Nancy Loomis and Gerald Loomis, husband and wife, and as personal representatives of the Estate of Kelly Loomis, Plaintiff, v. City of Puyallup Police Department, a municipal corporation; Ambrose J. Seitz and “Jane Doe” Seitz, husband and wife; and Rodger Cool and “Jane Doe” Cool, husband and wife, Defendants
Piety Ann Clark, Respondent, v. Wayne A. Baines and Jane Doe Baines, husband and wife, Petitioners
questions: While maintaining his innocence, Wayne Baines pleaded guilty to charges that he assaulted Piety Clark. Subsequently Clark brought a lawsuit seeking damages for the assault. Baines argues Clark’s actions amount to malicious prosecution.

title: Zoe Philippides, as personal representative of the Estate of Yianni Philippides, Deceased, and Kathryn and George Philippides, wife and husband, Respondents, v. Robert Bernard, and Wolverine World Wide Inc., a Delaware corporation, Appellants, and Robert Johns, Defendant
questions: The parents in these four cases believe that the Legislature changed the rule in Washington that the parents of adult children can only recover for the loss of the companionship of their injured or deceased adult children if the parents were financially dependent on the children.

title: Thomas R. Dreiling, Respondent, v. Naveen Jain, et ux., et al., Respondents, And Infospace , a Delaware corporation, Nominal Defendant/Respondent, And The Seattle Times Company, Intervenor/Petitioner
questions: Whether the superior court in this shareholder derivative action properly entered a protective order allowing a report of the corporation's special litigation committee, and supporting documents, to be filed under seal.

title: Washington State Council Of County And City Employees, Council 2, AFSCME, AFL-CI, Local 87 And Local 87P, Petitioners, v. Susan Hahn, Presiding Judge, Yakima County Superior Court, And Ruth Reukauf, Presiding Judge, Yakima County District Court, Respondents
questions: Whether a court rule prohibits trial court judges from collectively bargaining with their employees?

title: In re 17502, Attorney at Law
questions: What is the appropriate sanction, if any, for an attorney who delays for 14 months the filing of his client's appellate brief, where the attorney promptly delivers the file to substitute counsel and where the delay has no effect on the outcome of the client's appeal?

title: State v. State
questions: Whether the Pollution Control Hearings Board properly imposed conditions upon (and, as conditioned, properly affirmed) a water quality certification issued by the Department of Ecology for the Third Runway Project at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport.

title: Fortune View Condominium Association, Plaintiff, v. questions: A general contractor brought breach of warranty and implied indemnity claims against the manufacturer of an allegedly defective siding system used in the construction of a condominium project. The court must decide whether express warranties made through advertising can form the basis of an implied indemnity claim.

title: State v. Heritage
questions: To protect a suspect’s constitutional right not to make incriminating confessions or admissions while in custodial interrogation by police, the Supreme Court developed warnings that an officer must give prior to interrogation. The warnings are commonly referred to as Miranda warnings. The court decides whether a suspect’s right to Miranda warnings extends to custodial interrogation by a city park security officer.

title: State v. Tuupo
questions: Should a juvenile that commits certain acts when he is 15, but is not charged until after he is 16, be automatically declined by the juvenile court and tried in adult court? Did the State violate the defendant’s due process rights by delaying prosecution until after the defendant was 18?

title: State v. State
